record.original_question: For a virtual link with minimal classical crossing number C, minimal virtual crossing number V, and minimal total crossing number T, determine how C, V, and T are related, whether T = V + L in the notation of the paper, how the virtual unknotting number behaves, how V relates to minimal genus in a surface representation, and what effective algorithms or polynomial bounds exist for computing or estimating these quantities.

evidence.quote: For each virtual link L, there are three crossing numbers: the minimal number C of classical crossings, the minimal number V of virtual crossings, and the minimal total number T of crossings for representatives of L.
Very little is known. Find out more about the virtual unknotting number.
What is the relationship between the least number of virtual crossings and the least genus in a surface representation of the virtual knot.
Is it true that T = V + L?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A virtual link is an equivalence class of decorated 4-valent plane diagrams whose crossings are of two kinds — classical (over/under) and virtual (a small circled transverse intersection) — taken modulo the generalized Reidemeister moves (the three classical Reidemeister moves, the four purely virtual Reidemeister moves, and the mixed "detour" move). Equivalently, a virtual link can be represented as an embedded link in a thickened orientable closed surface Σ × [0,1], taken up to ambient isotopy and stabilization/destabilization of Σ.

For a virtual link L, define three crossing-number invariants:
 • C(L) = the minimum number of classical crossings over all diagrams of L;
 • V(L) = the minimum number of virtual crossings over all diagrams of L;
 • T(L) = the minimum total number of crossings (classical plus virtual) over all diagrams of L.
Define also the virtual unknotting number u_v(L) of a virtual knot L as the minimum, over all diagrams D of L, of the number of classical crossing changes needed to convert D into a diagram of the trivial knot (where virtual moves are allowed freely between changes). Finally, let g(L) denote the minimal genus of an orientable closed surface Σ such that L admits a representative as a link in Σ × [0,1] that is non-trivial in the sense of stabilization (the virtual genus).

Investigate the following:

(a) Determine the precise relationships among C(L), V(L), and T(L). In particular, decide whether the equality
  T(L) = C(L) + V(L)
holds for every virtual link L.

(b) Establish nontrivial lower and upper bounds on u_v(L) and describe its qualitative behavior (e.g., additivity under connected sum, comparison with the classical unknotting number when L is classical, realizability of arbitrary positive integers).

(c) Determine the relationship between V(L) and g(L); in particular, find sharp inequalities relating these two invariants.

(d) Exhibit effective algorithms or polynomial-time computable bounds (in the size of a given diagram) for estimating C(L), V(L), T(L), and u_v(L).
artifact.status_search_result: A web search returned foundational and recent works on virtual knot theory (Kauffman; Manturov; results on virtual crossing number estimates and on unknotting operations for virtual/welded knots), but none establishes the equality T = C + V in general, gives a complete description of the virtual unknotting number, or provides a sharp relation between V and the virtual genus. Partial bounds (e.g., polynomial-invariant lower bounds on V) and special cases exist, so the package of questions is best classified as open with partial progress.

status_evidence.title: Virtual Knot Theory — Kauffman
status_evidence.snippet: Foundational definitions of virtual links and crossing-number invariants; lists open questions about virtual crossing numbers and virtual unknotting number.
status_evidence.claim: The crossing-number invariants C, V, T and the virtual unknotting number are introduced as objects with limited known structure.

status_evidence.title: On Virtual Crossing Number Estimates for Virtual Links
status_evidence.snippet: Provides lower-bound estimates on the minimal number of virtual crossings using polynomial invariants of flat virtual knots.
status_evidence.claim: Only partial bounds on V(L) are known; no sharp formula relating V(L) to genus is established.

status_evidence.title: Unknotting operations for classical, virtual and welded knots (Chen, MSc thesis)
status_evidence.snippet: Surveys unknotting operations in the virtual setting; many basic questions about the virtual unknotting number remain unresolved.
status_evidence.claim: The virtual unknotting number is not fully understood and its general behavior remains open.
